title: Copy a Gene, Then Rewire It

scenes.tts: A human has 518 protein kinases. Baker's yeast has roughly 120 to 130. Animals share a short list of signaling pathways, so where did the extra parts come from? The record does not show animals inventing one new pathway after another. Kinase totals roughly track genome size, but the receptors multiplied more than the core.
scenes.visual: Two bars: human 518 kinases, yeast roughly 120 to 130. The human bar's extra length is a dashed box with a question mark. Ghost 'new pathway' chips are crossed out, then a receptors chip with a big arrow and a core-kinases chip with a smaller one.

scenes.tts: Mistakes in copying DNA sometimes duplicate a single gene. Say a receptor gene is copied. The original keeps doing the job, so the spare copy is free to change. A fly has one E G F receptor and a human has four. Jawed vertebrates carry traces of two whole genome doublings, the likely route from one to four.
scenes.caption: Mistakes in copying DNA sometimes duplicate a single gene. Say a receptor gene is copied. The original keeps doing the job, so the spare copy is free to change. A fly has one EGF receptor and a human has four. Jawed vertebrates carry traces of two whole genome doublings, the likely route from one to four.
scenes.visual: One receptor gene chip is copied; the original is labelled as keeping the job, the spare as free to change. Then a fly with one EGF receptor and a human whose single chip doubles twice, labelled as the likely route.

scenes.tts: A spare copy has three main fates. The common one is loss. A mutation disables the copy, nothing selects against that, and it decays into a pseudogene. In the second fate, the copies divide the old job. Suppose the old receptor worked in gut and in nerve. If one copy loses the regulatory DNA for gut and the other loses it for nerve, the animal needs both.
scenes.visual: Fate 1: the spare copy greys out and is crossed, labelled pseudogene. Everything is cleared for fate 2: an old receptor with gut and nerve tags is copied; one copy loses the gut tag, the other loses the nerve tag.

scenes.tts: In the third fate, one copy takes a new job. Its tail may change, so a different set of tyrosines recruits different S H 2 proteins. A docking site is only a few amino acids. The S H 2 domains of P I 3 kinase read a phosphotyrosine followed three positions later by methionine. One or two point mutations in the tail can make such a site, and with it a line to P I 3 kinase.
scenes.caption: In the third fate, one copy takes a new job. Its tail may change, so a different set of tyrosines recruits different SH2 proteins. A docking site is only a few amino acids. The SH2 domains of PI 3-kinase read a phosphotyrosine followed three positions later by methionine. One or two point mutations in the tail can make such a site, and with it a line to PI 3-kinase.
scenes.visual: A receptor tail as a row of boxes. PI 3-kinase hovers above with a two-pronged reader that wants phosphotyrosine and, three boxes later, methionine. The third box is blank; it changes to M and the reader drops in and closes.

scenes.tts: Now carry the duplication through a whole pathway. In one outcome, everything downstream is copied too, and the four cascades stay apart like four wires. In the other, the receptors go on sharing downstream parts and gain cross-connections. Many inputs then funnel into a few hubs, and Ras is one. The counts fit shared wiring, but they cannot show it, and the core was copied too.
scenes.visual: Four receptors each with their own two kinases: four wires. Cleared and replaced: all four feed one Ras hub and shared kinases, with cross-links between neighbours.
scenes.narration: Now carry the duplication through a whole pathway. In one outcome, everything downstream is copied too, and the four cascades stay apart like four wires. scenes.tts: So the extra kinases are not a list of new pathways. The record shows old pathways copied, mostly at the receptor end, and the copies changed. New wiring can cost only a few amino acids, because signaling proteins are built from parts that work on their own. Keep this rule: old pathways get copied, and the copies get rewired.
scenes.visual: The two bars return. The question-mark box fills with blue copies, each carrying a yellow changed mark, and a few amino acids label points at one.
